core_obligations: Reduce the claim to conditions (1) and (2) of the initial criterion, condition (1) being immediate (proof lines 2795-2797).

Assume condition (2) fails and choose a minimal element $i : Z \to X$ of the collection of reduced irreducible closed subspaces for which $i_*\mathcal{I}$ fails $\mathcal{P}$ for some quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_Z$ (proof lines 2798-2811).

Take the sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ supplied by assumption (3), form the injection $\varphi : i_*\mathcal{I}^{\oplus r} \to \mathcal{G}$ and filter its cokernel by the coherent filter lemma; by minimality and condition (1) the cokernel has $\mathcal{P}$, whence $i_*\mathcal{I}^{\oplus r}$, and by condition (2) also $i_*\mathcal{I}$, has $\mathcal{P}$ (proof lines 2813-2827).

For a second ideal $\mathcal{J}$ put $\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{I} \cap \mathcal{J}$ and use the two short exact sequences together with minimality and condition (1) to obtain $\mathcal{P}$ for $i_*\mathcal{K}$ and then for $i_*\mathcal{J}$, contradicting the choice of $Z$ (proof lines 2829-2845).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the initial criterion (proof lines 2795-2797).
The injection from an ideal power into the supplied sheaf and its cokernel (proof lines 2813-2827).
The second ideal and the contradiction (proof lines 2829-2845).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a variant of the earlier criterion: instead of demanding a supply of subsheaves of each ideal multiple, it asks for a single coherent sheaf with prescribed scheme theoretic support satisfying the property, and concludes the property for all coherent sheaves (statement lines 2778-2793). The proof discharges the two conditions of the initial criterion, the second by a minimal counterexample among reduced irreducible subspaces, comparing the ideal powers with the supplied sheaf through the preparation and filtration lemmas, and closing with an intersection argument for two ideals. The minimal counterexample comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
